links.outcome: Physician decision accuracy and speed with versus without the LLM assistant
links.effect: Physicians using HCC-STAR as an assistant made more accurate decisions faster; the model also surpassed resident and attending physicians in treatment accuracy. No numbers in abstract.
links.quote: The model surpassed resident and attending physicians in treatment accuracy and helped physicians make more accurate decisions faster when used as an assistant.

links.outcome: Treatment recommendation and risk stratification versus guidelines and competing models
links.effect: HCC-STAR achieved state-of-the-art performance versus clinical guidelines (BCLC, CNLC) and competitive models including GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 Pro in 6,668 patients from 12 hospitals.
links.quote: In a multi-center cohort of 6,668 patients from 12 hospitals in China, HCC-STAR achieved state-of-the-art performance in treatment recommendation and risk stratification compared with clinical guidelines and competitive models, including GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 Pro.

unlisted_practices: Step-verifiable composite reward training to align LLM reasoning with clinical guidelines
Clinician-validated synthetic EMR narrative data augmentation

screen.reason: The study evaluates a specialized LLM (HCC-STAR) on clinical decision support for hepatocellular carcinoma, including clinician-centric evaluations testing physician decision accuracy and speed with vs without AI assistance.
